gen-gf-gugi-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada reads with tall, full-bodied s and z shapes and a line that never swells or thins, every curve left open at its end. Gugi's chunky display heading sits above it, and a long page would still flow easily.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-radio-ca: Expressive, with a hand-lettered looseness that never jumps in weight. Radio Canada Big follows underneath as a tidy monoline sans-serif, its large x-height filling each line so Love Ya Like A Sister can be the only one making noise.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-rowan: Round, chunky, impossible to miss. Autour One has no tilted stress in its curves, while Rowan underneath shows a slight but noticeable swing from thick to thin strokes, giving the page a gentle bookish counterweight.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-almendra: Almendra reads dignified and bookish, with a deep midsection that gives each lowercase word some weight. Over a long stretch, Almendra settles into a slow, old-fashioned rhythm, while Autour One stays out of its way above.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-bree-serif: Bree Serif reads refined, its lowercase oversized and easy to pick out. Autour One is best at announcing things with a bold, gently uniform line, whereas Bree Serif is best at carrying the words that follow.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-port-lligat-slab: Autour One looks drawn with a compass and pencil, each round letter fed by a clear channel and no hairline shift. Port Lligat Slab continues in a traditional, literary voice, its wide portholes of counters keeping a long passage unhurried.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-quando: Bookish, with sparse, wide-set letters and a big middle zone in every word. Autour One does best at bold, monoline statements from start to finish, while Quando is happiest in traditional running text.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-dm-sans: Balsamiq Sans holds the same stencil-cut weight through every turn, with no pinched curves anywhere. DM Sans follows as a friendly sans-serif, its wide-set terminals on the s giving the heading a relaxed partner.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-paquito: Paquito sits confident and approachable, with barely any gap between its lowercase and its capitals. And Balsamiq Sans, with horizontals as thick as its verticals, hands over to it so a long page reads steadily.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-aleo: Aleo reads dignified and classic, its counters letting the eye slip in and out of each letter. And if Balsamiq Sans is made small, its constant weight loses some of its bold presence, so the body gets the quiet job.
